description: This phase explores teenage experiences (ages 13-19) to understand identity formation, social dynamics, academic ambition, resilience, values, and decision-making patterns that shape who the user is becoming.

categories.name: Identity Formation
categories.description: Understanding self-concept, personal identity, self-esteem, authenticity, and identity development
categories.source: SUNY Identity Formation, Handbook of Adolescent Psychology, MDPI Review, IJRAR Study

questions.direct_question: Tell me about yourself. What do you think makes you, you?
questions.story_hook: Imagine someone meeting you for the very first time.

questions.direct_question: What is something about yourself that you're genuinely proud of?
questions.memory_hook: Think about a moment when you felt proud of yourself.

questions.direct_question: When do you feel most like your true self?
questions.reflection_hook: Think about moments when you feel completely comfortable being yourself.

questions.direct_question: What do you think has changed the most about you over the last few years?
questions.story_hook: Think about who you were a few years ago compared to today.

questions.direct_question: What kind of person do you hope to become?
questions.scenario_hook: Imagine yourself five years from now.

questions.direct_question: What values are most important to you today?
questions.purpose: Understanding personal values and identity commitment

questions.direct_question: Can you remember a moment that made you see yourself differently?
questions.memory_hook: Think about an experience that changed the way you looked at yourself.

questions.direct_question: What motivates you to keep trying when something feels difficult?
questions.memory_hook: Think about a challenge you didn't give up on.

questions.direct_question: What part of your personality do you think has stayed the same since you were younger?
questions.memory_hook: Think about what your family used to say about you growing up.

questions.direct_question: Is there something you're still trying to figure out about yourself?
questions.reflection_hook: It's okay if you're still discovering who you are.

questions.direct_question: What achievement has made you feel the most confident in yourself?
questions.story_hook: Tell me about a moment when you felt you could do something important.

questions.direct_question: Have your dreams or goals changed as you've grown older?
questions.memory_hook: Think about what you wanted when you were younger.

questions.direct_question: If you had to describe yourself using just one word, what would it be?
What personal quality do you value most in yourself?
What experience has taught you the most about who you are?
questions.purpose: Understanding identity formation through life experiences
questions.story_hook: Think about an experience you'll probably remember for a long time.

categories.name: Social Dynamics & Relationships
categories.description: Understanding peer relationships, social integration, belonging, and communication patterns
categories.source: Peer Relationships, Social Adjustment, Social Media & Peer Influence

questions.direct_question: Who do you usually enjoy spending time with, and what makes those relationships special?
questions.purpose: Understanding meaningful peer relationships and social preferences
questions.story_hook: Think about the people you enjoy being around the most.

questions.direct_question: Can you tell me about a time when a friend positively influenced you?
Have you ever felt pressured to do something because everyone else was doing it? What happened?
When you disagree with your friends, how do you usually handle the situation?
Who do you usually talk to when you're having a difficult day?
questions.purpose: Understanding support systems and help-seeking behavior

questions.direct_question: Tell me about a moment when you felt you truly belonged somewhere.
What qualities do you appreciate most in a good friend?
Can you remember a time when someone made you feel included?
How comfortable are you expressing your thoughts when you're with other people?
Have you ever changed something about yourself to fit in with a group?
What makes you feel respected by other people?
questions.purpose: Understanding interpersonal expectations and healthy relationships

questions.direct_question: Can you describe a time when helping someone made you feel good?
How do you usually respond when someone has a different opinion from yours?
questions.purpose: Understanding respect, communication, and social flexibility

questions.direct_question: Has social media ever changed the way you interact with your friends?
If you could improve one thing about the way you connect with other people, what would it be?
questions.purpose: Understanding self-awareness in social relationships and future social growth

categories.name: Academic Ambition & Learning
categories.description: Understanding intrinsic motivation, goal-setting, academic resilience, and learning aspirations
categories.source: Academic Motivation Scale, Frontiers in Psychology, Academic Resilience Review

questions.direct_question: What is something you genuinely enjoy learning about, and what makes it interesting to you?
questions.purpose: Understanding intrinsic motivation and curiosity for learning

questions.direct_question: Can you tell me about a goal you're currently working towards in school or your personal learning?
questions.purpose: Understanding academic goal setting and aspirations

questions.direct_question: Think about a time when learning something difficult felt worth the effort. What kept you going?
What does doing well in school mean to you personally?
questions.purpose: Understanding personal meaning attached to academic success

questions.direct_question: When you don't understand something in class, what do you usually do next?
Can you describe a moment when you felt proud of something you achieved through learning?
How do you stay motivated when a subject feels difficult or uninteresting?
If you could become really good at one skill before finishing school, what would it be, and why?
What usually inspires you to put extra effort into your studies?
questions.purpose: Understanding internal and external sources of motivation

questions.direct_question: Tell me about a time when you didn't perform as well as you expected. What did you learn from that experience?
How do you usually decide which tasks or assignments to complete first?
Who has encouraged or inspired you the most in your learning journey?
questions.purpose: Understanding the influence of mentors, teachers, and family on academic ambition

questions.direct_question: If you could change one thing about the way you learn, what would it be?
What kind of future do you hope your education will help you build?
questions.purpose: Understanding educational aspirations and future orientation

questions.direct_question: Looking back over the past year, what is one lesson—inside or outside the classroom—that has helped you grow the most?
questions.purpose: Understanding learning, personal growth, and academic development

categories.name: Resilience & Coping
categories.description: Understanding emotional regulation, coping strategies, perseverance, adaptability, and self-efficacy
categories.source: ARES-i25, Emotion Regulation Research, Systematic Review on Resilience

questions.direct_question: Can you tell me about a challenge you faced recently and how you got through it?
When something doesn't go the way you expected, what usually helps you move forward?
Who do you usually turn to when you're having a difficult time, and what makes them someone you trust?
Can you think of a difficult experience that taught you something valuable about yourself?
When you start feeling overwhelmed, what do you usually do to calm yourself?
Can you describe a time when you surprised yourself by handling something better than you expected?
What personal strength do you think helps you most when life becomes challenging?
Have you ever had to adjust your plans because something unexpected happened? How did you handle it?
What keeps you going when you feel like giving up?
When you make a mistake or fail at something important, how do you usually respond?
Can you share a moment when someone encouraged you during a difficult time? How did it affect you?
questions.purpose: Understanding the role of encouragement and emotional support

questions.direct_question: How do you usually remind yourself that things can get better during tough times?
If a close friend was going through a difficult situation, how would you support them?
questions.purpose: Understanding empathy, social resilience, and interpersonal coping

questions.direct_question: Looking back over the past year, what challenge has helped you grow the most as a person?
questions.purpose: Understanding long-term resilience and personal growth

questions.direct_question: What advice would you give your younger self about dealing with difficult situations?
questions.purpose: Understanding resilience, wisdom gained through experience, and self-reflection

categories.name: Values & Morality
categories.description: Understanding personal values, moral reasoning, responsibility, fairness, and integrity
categories.source: Life Values and Adolescent Mental Health, Hart & Carlo — Moral Development

questions.direct_question: What qualities do you admire most in another person, and why?
questions.purpose: Understanding admired values and role-model influences

questions.direct_question: Can you tell me about a time when doing the right thing wasn't the easiest choice?
questions.purpose: Understanding moral reasoning and ethical decision-making

questions.direct_question: What does being a good person mean to you?
Have you ever changed your mind about what was important to you? What influenced that change?
When two important things matter to you at the same time, how do you usually decide what to do first?
Who has had the biggest influence on the values you hold today?
questions.purpose: Understanding family, peer, and environmental influences

questions.direct_question: Can you remember a moment when you stood up for something you believed was right?
What does being a responsible person mean to you?
How do you decide whether something is fair or unfair?
Tell me about a time when you admitted making a mistake. What happened afterward?
questions.purpose: Understanding honesty, accountability, and ethical responsibility

questions.direct_question: If a friend asked you to do something that didn't feel right to you, how would you handle it?
What kind of person do you hope people remember you as?
questions.purpose: Understanding long-term values and moral identity

questions.direct_question: Can you share a time when helping someone else made you feel good about yourself?
What is one value you think young people today should never lose, and why?
questions.purpose: Understanding societal values and personal beliefs

questions.direct_question: Looking back over the past year, what experience has strengthened your values the most?
questions.purpose: Understanding how experiences shape values and character

categories.name: Decision Making & Problem Solving
categories.description: Understanding decision-making processes, risk assessment, peer influence, and long-term thinking
categories.source: Decision Making in Adolescents, Risk and Rationality, General Decision Making Style Questionnaire

questions.direct_question: Can you tell me about an important decision you made recently and how you arrived at that choice?
questions.purpose: Understanding the adolescent's overall decision-making process

questions.direct_question: When you're faced with several choices, what helps you decide which option is best?
How much time do you usually spend thinking before making an important decision?
Can you describe a time when thinking carefully changed the decision you were about to make?
questions.purpose: Understanding thoughtful reasoning and cognitive control

questions.direct_question: How do you usually think about the possible consequences before making an important choice?
Has there ever been a situation where your friends influenced a decision you made? What happened?
When you're unsure about a decision, what usually helps you feel more confident?
Can you think of a decision that didn't turn out the way you expected? What did you learn from it?
questions.purpose: Understanding reflection and learning from experience

questions.direct_question: When you need to make a difficult decision, do you usually rely more on facts, your feelings, or advice from others? Why?
How do you decide whether taking a risk is worth it?
questions.purpose: Understanding risk perception and reward evaluation

questions.direct_question: Can you tell me about a time when you changed your mind after hearing someone else's perspective?
questions.purpose: Understanding flexibility and openness to new information

questions.direct_question: What do you usually do when you don't have enough information to make a decision?
Have you ever had to choose between something that felt good immediately and something that would benefit you later? How did you decide?
questions.purpose: Understanding delayed gratification and long-term thinking

questions.direct_question: When you're feeling stressed or emotional, how does it affect the decisions you make?
Looking back over the past year, which decision are you most proud of, and what made it the right choice for you?
questions.purpose: Understanding self-reflection, judgment, and personal decision quality

follow_up_strategies.if_emotional: That sounds really meaningful. What do you think that experience taught you about yourself?
follow_up_strategies.if_brief: I'm curious about that—what made that so significant to you?
follow_up_strategies.if_resistant: That's okay. We can come back to it later if you'd prefer. Let's try another question.
follow_up_strategies.if_reflective: That's a beautiful way to put it. What do you think that says about who you are today?
follow_up_strategies.if_general: That's interesting. Can you tell me more about that?
follow_up_strategies.if_hesitant: Take your time. Sometimes the best answers come when we let them find us.
follow_up_strategies.if_surprising: That's fascinating—I didn't expect that. What do you think made you feel that way?
